Scene context: Two people stand behind a flower-arranging table with separate unfinished bouquets. Their separate hands hold the same tulip stem at different heights; the woman uses supplied face and bob reference.

A photographic romantic comedy moment in a sunny neighborhood flower-arranging hobby club: two hobby-club rivals discover mutual attraction during a playful contest. The woman based on the supplied reference is on the left, preserving the reference woman's soft oval face, large dark eyes, rose lips, and short dark bob with wispy bangs. A fictional male rival with wavy dark hair and an open, boyish smile stands on the right. Their competitive encounter turns flirtatious. Two equally extravagant, unfinished bouquets stand in separate heavy glass vases on a broad wooden worktable, each with an obvious empty gap waiting for the final red tulip. Both competitors have reached for that same tulip at once and stopped. Her right hand gently encircles the upper bare stem below the leaves; his left hand encircles the lower bare stem, with a clear section of continuous green stem visible between their separate hands. The single red flower rises above the shared grip. Her left palm rests on the table beside her own vase and his free right hand rests beside his arrangement. Both bodies remain comfortably upright behind the table. She raises one eyebrow at him, trying to keep a mock-serious competitive face while an involuntary smile breaks through; he looks directly back at her, visibly amused and a little caught off guard. Their attention has left the flower for each other, while both still politely refuse to release it. Photograph the pair from hip level upward at an oblique front angle, faces, shared stem and both vases forming one readable triangle. Natural window light, fresh stems and scattered cut leaves, warm skin, honest facial texture, a candid film-still feeling and gently restrained color. Her simple pale-blue sleeveless knit top and his rolled white shirt belong naturally to a weekend workshop.

Scene context: Outdoor winter-festival ice rink; the staged graceful date photograph has just been interrupted. The protagonist follows the supplied face-and-hair reference.

Scene context: They stand close to the rink rail with joined hands between separate bodies; the playful embarrassment follows a small balance mishap.

A candid romantic-comedy photograph, a winter-festival romantic comedy in which the reference-guided protagonist shares an affectionate comic interaction with her date. Use the supplied reference as a visible face-and-hair appearance guide for the woman: retain her dark chin-length bob with wispy bangs, wide brown eyes, softly rounded cheeks and small softly shaped lips. Her clothing and the fictional situation are newly staged. At a small outdoor ice rink beside a Christmas market, she and a curly-haired man have stopped near the rink rail to attempt an elegant skating-date photograph. Instead, her left skate has slid sideways and she catches his offered right hand, her torso tipping toward him while her free right hand braces the wooden rail. His left hand grips the same rail behind his hip and his planted skates form a wide, awkward V; the effort to steady her has pulled his shoulders toward her. Their joined hands sit visibly between their separate bodies, each arm traceable from shoulder to grip. Both pairs of skates remain on the ice. She looks directly at his face with a startled open smile; he meets her gaze with a helpless laugh, one eyebrow raised at his own ungainly rescue. Their faces hover closer than the composed portrait they meant to take, and their mutual attraction lives in that involuntary shared amusement. She wears a cranberry wool coat over a cream knit dress with winter tights and white rental skates; he wears a forest-green coat, a mustard scarf and black rental skates. The scarf has swung sideways with his turn, reinforcing the interrupted balance. Behind them, a narrow row of softly glowing market huts, evergreen garlands and one blurred skating couple establishes the seasonal outing. Frame their full bodies and the uninterrupted hand-to-hand connection at a three-quarter side angle, with the woman's face turned enough toward camera to retain the reference features. A 40mm photographic perspective, crisp eyes and hands, gently softened festive background, blue-hour air and warm kiosk spill light keep the playful rescue and their caught-off-guard closeness foremost. The image feels like a believable instant of a date going endearingly wrong.

A naturalistic photographic romantic-comedy scene, a chance encounter in which a comic mishap softens into mutual attraction. The woman guided by the attached reference has its chin-length dark bob and wispy center fringe; preserve the reference woman's large brown eyes, soft oval face, small straight nose and softly full pink lips. Use this face-and-hair appearance in a newly staged scene. At the edge of a sidewalk cafe just after rain, she is closing a cream cafe parasol beside an outdoor table when the last collected water spills from its low scalloped rim onto the near shoulder of a neatly dressed man passing beside her. Show the short falling trail of drops and a fresh dark wet patch on his tan jacket together beneath that canopy edge. Her right hand remains on the parasol's waist-height closing crank, connected to its upright pole; her left hand extends a folded white napkin toward his wet shoulder across the gap between them. He has paused with both feet on the pavement, shoulders pulled up at the cold surprise, one open hand lifted beside his jacket. His raised eyebrow and crooked, involuntary grin answer her embarrassed laugh; their eyes meet, and she leans forward slightly as if an apology has just escaped into laughter. Their mutual attention and easy closeness suggest a new attraction amid a small public embarrassment. She wears a pale blue short-sleeve blouse and a black A-line skirt, with rain-softened strands near her cheek. Photograph both people from mid-thigh upward at eye level in a horizontal frame, their faces and distinct hands large enough to read, the parasol edge above the wet shoulder forming a clear triangle with the offered napkin. Retain a little sidewalk and cafe seating in the background. Soft light after the shower, natural skin texture, restrained color, a candid still from an intimate city comedy; focus joins both faces and the small watery mishap in the same plane.
